summary: A 1970 note with more comments on the forthcoming protocol, by the same authors as RFC 39. It continues discussion about the proposed host-to-host protocol before it was finalised.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 40 adds detail to earlier host-to-host protocol discussions. It proposes formats for error reports and connection queries, plus a message that can announce an NCP's availability.

questions: more comments on the forthcoming protocol
what did rfc 40 propose for protocol errors
how did early ncp queries work
subtitle: Proposals for protocol error messages, connection queries, and NCP host status.

tldr.problem: The forthcoming host-to-host protocol needed more detail about reporting errors, querying connection state, and tracking host availability.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 40 proposes an error message containing a code and the command in error, a query/reply with connection-table entries, and a NOP message for host status.
tldr.outcome: This memo provides proposals and discussion for the forthcoming protocol; it does not report a finalized design.

sections.title: Error Messages
sections.content:
The proposed error message contains an error code, the length of the command in error, and the command itself. The error code is eight bits, and the command-length field is a 16-bit integer measured in bits.

Examples include code 01 for a request for an invalid resource, code 02 for an exhausted resource, code 20 for an unknown command code, and code 21 for a message received on an unconnected link.
sections.plainLanguage: An error report identifies the error type and includes the command that caused it. Codes distinguish conditions such as an invalid resource request or an unknown command.

sections.title: Connection Queries and Replies
sections.content:
The proposed QRY message includes the sender's socket. An RPY response includes the other socket and text containing a count of relevant connection-table entries followed by those entries.

Each entry contains local and foreign socket information, link and connection state, flow and buffer control, and reconnection control state.
sections.plainLanguage: A host can ask another host for information about relevant connections. The reply lists connection details such as sockets, links, and state.

sections.title: NCP Availability
sections.content:
The note proposes a NOP command for host status. When an NCP changes its state to UP, it should send NOP to each remote NCP to announce availability.

A receiving NCP can use that notice to update its host-status information. The sending NCP can also build a status vector from the RFNMs it receives.
sections.plainLanguage: An NCP that becomes available can notify remote NCPs with a NOP. Receiving hosts can use that notice to update their host-status records.
